column4: A single empty instant photo print from the late 1990s scanned flat on a plain white background and seen straight on: the classic white frame of an instant photo, its bottom border much wider than the other three, the square picture area in the middle filled with flat even mid grey; the frame a little yellowed with age, a faint grey thumbprint smudge on the wide bottom border, one tiny crease at a corner, real glossy photo paper texture with very fine grain. No text, no logo, no picture in the grey square, nothing else in the image.

Separate quick marks drawn by hand with a thick red felt-tip marker on plain white paper, scanned flat and evenly lit: two curved arrows of different lengths with simple open heads, one loose circle, one rough oval, one cross made of two strokes, one short wavy underline. Uneven ink, the strokes darker where the pen pressed and lighter where it ran dry, slightly soaked into the paper fibres, drawn fast by an old woman. Every mark far apart from the others with a lot of empty white paper between them. No letters, no numbers, no other drawing, no shadow.
